VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 11, 2024
  6615 PACIFIC COAST HIGHWAY, LONG BEACH, 90803
  SUITE 180, 5:00 PM

Juanita Doplemore, Chair  James Goodin, Commissioner
Kenneth Osborn, Vice Chair  James Schotter, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Commissioner  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Doplemore called meeting to order at 5:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter

Commissioners Absent: Hill

Also present: Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

Also in attendance: Johnny Vallejo (Economic Development), Emma Vallejo, and Alexandria O’Bard.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Commissioner Schotter led the Pledge of Allegiance, which was followed by the Chair Report and
Staff Report.

 Chair report: outgoing Commission Chair (Doplemore) reflected on the “year gone by like a C-130,”
highlighting the various events and activities in which the Commission and the Office of Veterans
participated or played key roles, including the Veteran Town Hall, the Veterans Banners program and
its renewal for FY 2025, the Memorial Day and Veterans Day events, the Lone Sailor commemoration
and the Veteran Stand Down, as well as more engagement with the Veterans community and service
providers via advocacy on behalf of homeless Veterans and more. Staff report: Commission staff
(Overholt) outlined the meeting, and acknowledged the presentation and discussion (at November’s
meeting) about the 1400 Cherry project.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-55883  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of November 13, 2024

  A motion was made by Commissioner Schotter, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

2.  24-55884  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the new Housing-
  Related Subcommittee

  Commissioner Doplemore leads this subcommittee, heretofore referred to as the
  Veteran Housing and Homeless subcommittee. She acknowledged last month’s
  presentation by developers who are proposing a Veteran-focused housing
  development (1400 Cherry). A next step is to draft a letter of support for the project.
  Discussion followed. The Commission concluded that it is too early for such a letter;
  the project is in the architectural design phase. It may be more effective to submit a
  letter once the project is vetted by the Planning Bureau and on the Community
  Development Commission’s agenda. Commissioner Osborn will connect with the
  project lead on progress. Commissioner Sramek shared that 150 additional units of
  Veteran-focused housing is planned for American Gold Star Manor.

  Second component of this item: Commissioner Schotter noted that connecting
  homeless Veterans with temporary shelter may take 24 to 36 hours because they
  must be verified by the VA for GPD funding. If a Veteran in need were connected
  directly with the City’s Homeless Services Bureau, the Veteran could be housed in
  less time. This would only involve some communication and training of staffers for
  the City’s resources lines. Commission staff will work with the subcommittee to
  explore next steps.

  During public comment on this item, speakers concurred that we need to know
  more about the project before writing a letter of support, and about the need to
  temporarily house homeless Veterans more quickly with the nearest VA affiliated
  shelters in Inglewood and Tustin being more than 20 miles away.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goodin, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

3.  24-55885  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Veterans Banner Program

  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 11, 2024
  6615 PACIFIC COAST HIGHWAY, LONG BEACH, 90803

  A motion was made by Commissioner Schotter, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

  Subcommittee chair Osborn reported on progress, including the drafting and
  reviewing the nomination form as well as the selection criteria, and the need for
  outreach to ensure a diverse pool of nominees for the program. Discussion followed
  on potential locations for the banners in multiple Council districts and potentially at
  the VA campus, the latter of which will need to be explored with the City.
  Commissioner input is needed to put together a substantive list of locations to be
  vetted by Special Events.

4.  24-55886  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the End-of-Year Celebration
  on January 8, 2025

  The celebration will now take place at the Ron Arias Health Equity Center.
  Commissioners were encouraged to invite electeds and other VIPs; a save the date
  will be sent out. (A sign up sheet for side dishes and dessert was distributed). The
  Commission agreed to start the meeting at 4:30, with the celebration immediately
  following.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goodin, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

5.  24-55887  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on an MLK Day Service Project

  A substitute motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by
  Commissioner Atkins Blade, Substitute Motion to submit an application for an
  MLK Day (January 20) service project to Leadership Long Beach. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Page 3 of 5
   VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 11, 2024
  6615 PACIFIC COAST HIGHWAY, LONG BEACH, 90803
  SUITE 180, 5:00 PM

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

  Chair Doplemore suggested that the Commission propose an MLK Day service
  project, namely, the cleaning of Veterans’ headstones at the Municipal and
  Sunnyside Cemeteries. This would be submitted to Leadership Long Beach (LLB),
  which solicits and selects MLK Day service projects. Discussion followed. LLB
  presumably handles obtaining permission for the projects, in this case, from the
  City’s Parks, Recreation and Marine department.

6.  24-55888  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on additional volunteer position
  to support Commission

  A motion was made by Commissioner Goodin, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

  Commissioner Doplemore proposed that a third position be created, in addition to
  chair and vice chair, to assist with administrative-related tasks, such as minutes and
  ensuring quorum for meetings. This would be an appointed position and offer an
  opportunity for a Commissioner to be more actively engaged. Discussion followed.
  These responsibilities may be taken on by the vice chair. No motion was taken.

7.  24-55889  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the 2025 Calendar

  The Commission reviewed a draft calendar for 2025 listing monthly Commission
  meeting dates, main event dates (for Memorial Day and Veterans Day) and dates
  TBD for the Veterans Banners program and other activities.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Osborn, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6 Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter

CHAIR AND VICE CHAIR ELECTION

Chair Doplemore opened the floor for nominations for Chair and Vice Chair. The nominees made
statements, after which the election was conducted. Commissioner Osborn was elected Chair and
Commissioner Atkins Blade was elected Vice Chair.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

CD 5 Councilmember Megan Kerr, working with the Long Beach Veterans Collaborative, is holding a
Veterans Donation drive through December 27, with drop off locations throughout CD 5. Items will be
distributed at locations where formerly homeless Veterans live, such as Century Villages at Cabrillo.

Future Agenda Items: MLK Day of Service, Housing & Homeless subcommittee (advocacy work),
Roberts Rules & Brown Act review

ADJOURNMENT

Outgoing Chair Doplemore adjourned the meeting at 6:53 p.m.
